$comment: IMPORTANT APPLICABILITY NOTE: Key Security Indicators (KSIs) are a FedRAMP 20x-specific standard (https://www.fedramp.gov/20x/standards/20x-ksi/). The standard explicitly states it 'does not apply to FedRAMP Rev 5 authorizations.' Overleaf's actual FedRAMP certification is Rev5 / Class B (Low) — formerly called the LI-SaaS baseline under the pre-2026 naming. So there is no official FedRAMP requirement or mechanism today that formally evaluates Overleaf against these KSIs, and nothing below should be read as an official FedRAMP determination. What follows is a SELF-ASSESSED, INFORMAL cross-reference — useful for forward-looking 20x readiness and for giving engineers/customers a sense of security posture, but not a substitute for the Rev5 SSP control set that is Overleaf's actual authorization basis. Theme list and validation items below are copied from the authoritative source (fetched 2026-09-23): https://www.fedramp.gov/20x/standards/20x-ksi/. Statuses are 'not-yet-evaluated' by default; only change a status to 'self-assessed-met' if there is a real, named piece of evidence for it (see 'evidence' field) — do not mark items met just because the class/baseline is low-risk.

results.description: A secure cloud service offering will use cloud native architecture and design principles to enforce and enhance Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability.
A secure cloud service offering will follow FedRAMP encryption policies, continuously verify information resource integrity, and restrict access to third-party information resources.
results.evidence: SVC-02 (encrypt/secure network traffic) and SVC-03 (encrypt federal/sensitive data at rest): Dan (2026-09-23) confirms encryption is in place both in transit and at rest. Specifics not yet documented here — TLS version/cipher suites, KMS/key management approach, and exactly which data stores are covered should be pulled from infra/security docs before citing this as full SVC-02/03 evidence in an official package. Does not cover SVC-01 (hardened configs), SVC-04 (central config management), SVC-05 (integrity via cryptographic means), SVC-06 (automated key rotation), or SVC-07 (patching approach) — those remain not-yet-evaluated.

results.description: A secure cloud service offering will protect user data, control access, and apply zero trust principles.
results.evidence: IAM-01 (phishing-resistant MFA): Dan (2026-09-23) confirms MFA is supported via SSO. Per the FedRAMP Customer Responsibility Matrix, MFA enforcement over a federated/SSO login is a SHARED control — the customer's own IdP is responsible for actually enforcing phishing-resistant MFA; Overleaf's role is supporting the SSO/SAML federation that carries it. So this is evidence that Overleaf enables the shared control, not that IAM-01 is fully met unilaterally — confirm with the security team whether any non-SSO/direct-login account paths (if they exist) have their own MFA requirement, since the shared-control answer only covers the SSO path. Does not cover IAM-02 (passwordless auth), IAM-03 (non-user/service account auth), IAM-04 (least-privilege/JIT model), IAM-05 (zero trust design), or IAM-06 (automated response to suspicious privileged-account activity) — those remain not-yet-evaluated.

results.description: A secure cloud service offering will monitor, log, and audit all important events, activity, and changes.
results.evidence: Authenticated web-app scanning sub-item (MLA-04): a Qualys WAS 'Discovery Scan' (target: stag-overleaf.com, run 06 Sep 2026, report generated 17 Sep 2026 by J. Lees-Miller) came back Low overall risk with 0 vulnerabilities at Levels 1-5 and 68 informational-only findings (mostly expected 403/404s from a link-discovery crawl). This is one data point for MLA-04 (vulnerability scanning) only — it does not establish MLA-01 (SIEM), MLA-02 (log review), MLA-03/06 (remediation tracking), or MLA-05 (IaC scanning). Also note: a 'Discovery Scan' is not the same as a full authenticated application scan — confirm scan type/depth before citing this as authenticated vulnerability scanning evidence.

results.description: A secure cloud service provider will ensure that all system changes are properly documented and configuration baselines are updated accordingly.
A secure cloud service offering will have intentional, organized, universal guidance for how every information resource, including personnel, is secured.
results.evidence: PIY-03 (vulnerability disclosure program): Dan (2026-09-23) confirms Overleaf runs a live VDP via HackerOne, with a second program on YesWeHack planned to roll out soon (not live yet as of 2026-09-23 — follow up to confirm go-live date and update this entry once it launches). Does not cover PIY-01 (asset/inventory), PIY-02 (security policies), PIY-04 (secure SDLC / CISA Secure by Design), PIY-05 (documented evaluation methodology), PIY-06 (dedicated security staff/budget), or PIY-07 (software supply chain risk documentation) — those remain not-yet-evaluated.

results.description: A secure cloud service offering will understand, monitor, and manage supply chain risks from third-party information resources.
A secure cloud service provider will continuously educate their employees on cybersecurity measures, testing them regularly.
A secure cloud service offering will define, maintain, and test incident response plan(s) and recovery capabilities.
A secure cloud service offering will document, report, and analyze security incidents.

openQuestion: TODO(Dan/security team), updated 2026-09-23: KSI-IAM, KSI-SVC and KSI-PIY now have one piece of named evidence each (SSO-based MFA as a shared control, encryption in transit/at rest, and the HackerOne VDP respectively), but each theme has several other validation items still unconfirmed — see each entry's 'evidence' field for exactly which sub-items remain open. Specific follow-ups: (1) confirm whether any non-SSO/direct-login accounts exist and what MFA they use, since the SSO answer only covers the federated path; (2) get the specific TLS version/cipher suite and KMS/key-rotation approach for SVC-02/03 so this isn't just a yes/no; (3) confirm the YesWeHack rollout date and update KSI-PIY once it's live; (4) KSI-CNA, KSI-MLA (beyond the one scan already logged), KSI-CMT, KSI-TPR, KSI-CED, KSI-RPL, and KSI-INR have no evidence at all yet. Remember: being on the Low/Class B/LI-SaaS baseline does not by itself satisfy any KSI, since KSIs are a separate, 20x-only framework Overleaf isn't formally assessed against — every status change here should trace to a real, named piece of evidence.
